title: Americans see democracy as a diminished example and want change without equal confidence that change is possible
source_unit: Pew Research Center spring 2026 Global Attitudes Survey and U.S. democracy analysis
geography: United States, with cross-national high-income-country comparison

observations.period: March 23-29, 2026; U.S. democracy as an example for other countries

denominator.unit: percent of U.S. adults in the Pew survey

used_to_be_good_example_not_recently.unit: percent saying the U.S. used to be a good example of democracy but has not been in recent years

currently_good_example.unit: percent saying the U.S. is a good example of democracy for other countries

democracy_dissatisfied.unit: percent dissatisfied with the way democracy is working in the U.S.

observations.method: Pew U.S. survey comparison of democracy evaluation and satisfaction; measures are public judgments, not institutional performance audits.
observations.uncertainty: Questions capture current evaluation and comparison with the past; they do not identify which events caused dissatisfaction or whether respondents favor the same reforms.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults; the source reports strong partisan differences in satisfaction and in whether the U.S. is viewed as a current democratic example.
observations.counterinterpretation: Dissatisfaction can reflect current political control, policy outcomes, economic conditions, democratic norms, or expectations; it does not imply withdrawal or rejection of democracy itself.

democrats_dissatisfied.unit: percent among Democrats and Democratic leaners

republicans_dissatisfied.unit: percent among Republicans and Republican leaners

observations.method: Descriptive party-group comparison in the same Pew survey; party identity is not treated as a causal mechanism.
observations.uncertainty: Partisan differences can reflect who controls government, issue priorities, identity, and survey timing. They do not show durable realignment, action, or policy demand.
observations.subgroup: Democrats/Democratic leaners and Republicans/Republican leaners; independents are not represented by these two contrasts.
observations.counterinterpretation: A person can be dissatisfied with democratic performance while supporting democratic institutions, voting, organizing, or seeking reform through them.

related_sources.claim: Pew's cross-national companion places U.S. democratic satisfaction below most high-income-country comparisons and reports a 2025-to-2026 decline.

boundary: This record measures democratic evaluation and satisfaction in public-attitude surveys. It does not establish institutional performance, legal change, causal polarization, reform feasibility, turnout, protest, voting, or rejection of democratic government.
